posts.title: ALTHIA opens a new clinical simulation wing in Malabe
posts.excerpt: Eight mock wards, high-fidelity manikins and a debrief suite give nursing and health science students hundreds of hours of hands-on practice before their first placement.
posts.author: ALTHIA Communications

body.text: The new clinical simulation wing at our Malabe campus opened this week, giving students a safe place to practise real procedures long before they meet their first patient.

The wing has eight mock wards set up like a working hospital, each with a high-fidelity patient manikin that breathes, talks and responds to treatment. Lecturers run scenarios from a control room, from a routine admission to a patient whose condition changes suddenly.
Practice that feels like the real thing

Every session ends in the debrief suite, where students watch their recording back with a lecturer and talk through what went well and what to change. It is the same approach used in leading teaching hospitals.
Students make their mistakes here, with a manikin, not on a ward. By the time they reach placement, the basics feel routine.
Who uses the wing

items: HND in Nursing and Higher Diploma in Nursing students, from their first semester
Health Science students for patient assessment and first aid
Short course learners on life support and patient care courses

body.text: Prospective students can see the wing at our next Open Day.

posts.title: Applications are now open for the February 2027 intake
posts.excerpt: Apply online in about ten minutes for nursing, psychology, biomedical science and health science programmes. There is no application fee.
posts.author: Admissions Office

body.text: Applications for our February 2027 intake are now open across all four programme areas: Nursing, Psychology, Biomedical Science and Health Science.
The online form takes about ten minutes. You can upload your documents as you go, and our admissions team replies within two working days.
Key dates
Not sure which course fits? Talk to our team on WhatsApp or come to our Open Day on 14 November.

posts.title: Nursing students begin clinical placements at Hemas Hospitals
posts.excerpt: Our first nursing cohort has started supervised placements at Hemas Hospitals in Wattala and Thalawathugoda.
posts.author: ALTHIA Communications

body.text: Our first cohort of nursing students has started supervised clinical placements at Hemas Hospitals in Wattala and Thalawathugoda.
Each student works alongside a registered nurse mentor and rotates through medical, surgical and outpatient units over the semester.
The placements are where the classroom and the simulation lab come together. Students see why every step matters.
Placements are a core part of every ALTHIA nursing programme, made possible by our partnership with Hemas.

posts.title: Psychology students lead a campus wellbeing week
posts.excerpt: Talks, quiet zones and drop-in sessions run by second-year psychology students reached over 600 students across the Malabe campus.
posts.author: Student Life

body.text: Second-year psychology students planned and ran this year’s campus wellbeing week, with talks, quiet zones and drop-in sessions open to every student in Malabe.
Sessions covered exam stress, sleep and how to support a friend who is struggling. The wellbeing pods were open all week for anyone who needed a quiet moment.
The project counts towards the students’ community practice module and was supervised by our counselling team.

posts.title: A new pathway to the Higher Diploma in Nursing with Deakin
posts.excerpt: Students can now study the Deakin-linked Higher Diploma in Nursing in Colombo, with the same curriculum and assessment standards.
posts.author: ALTHIA Communications

body.text: Students can now study the Higher Diploma in Nursing, delivered with Deakin University, at our Malabe campus.
The programme follows the same curriculum and assessment standards, with teaching from ALTHIA lecturers and clinical placements in Sri Lanka.
Applications for the February 2027 intake are open now.

posts.title: Biomedical labs add PCR and clinical chemistry analysers
posts.excerpt: New research-grade equipment means biomedical science students now train on the same machines used in hospital labs.
posts.author: ALTHIA Communications

body.text: Our biomedical science labs now have new PCR systems and clinical chemistry analysers, the same equipment used in hospital and research labs.
Students will use them from their second year for molecular diagnostics, haematology and clinical chemistry practicals, and for final-year research projects.

posts.title: Health science students run a free screening camp in Malabe
posts.excerpt: Over 300 residents had free blood pressure, blood sugar and BMI checks, with advice from students and supervising staff.
posts.author: Community Outreach

body.text: Health science students ran a one-day free health screening camp for residents around our Malabe campus.
More than 300 people had blood pressure, blood sugar and BMI checks, and anyone with a high reading was referred to a nearby clinic.
The camp is part of the community health module and will run again next year.

posts.title: Open Day: February 2027 intake
posts.excerpt: Tour the labs, meet our lecturers and get help with your application on the day.

body.text: Join us at the Malabe campus to see where you could be studying from February 2027.
On the day

items: Guided tours of the simulation wing, biomedical labs and counselling suites
Short talks on each programme area
One-to-one advice on entry requirements and fees

body.text: Bring a parent or friend. No registration needed, but letting us know helps us plan.

posts.title: World Mental Health Day public talk
posts.excerpt: Our psychology faculty and guest clinicians talk about mental health at work, with time for questions.

body.text: Mark World Mental Health Day with a public talk from our psychology faculty and guest clinicians.
The talk looks at mental health at work: how to spot early signs of stress, and what employers and colleagues can do to help. There will be time for questions at the end.
Open to students, parents and the public.

posts.title: Careers in allied health: online info session
posts.excerpt: Find out where a nursing, psychology, biomedical or health science qualification can take you, in Sri Lanka and abroad.

body.text: A one-hour online session for school leavers and parents on careers in allied health.
Lecturers from each programme area explain the roles graduates go into, in Sri Lanka and overseas, and what employers look for.
We will email the Zoom link after you register.

posts.title: Clinical skills workshop for school leavers
posts.excerpt: Try basic life support, take a pulse and work with a patient manikin in our simulation wing.

body.text: A hands-on morning for school leavers thinking about nursing or health science.
You will try basic life support, take vital signs and work through a simple ward scenario with a patient manikin, guided by our nursing lecturers.
Places are limited to 30, so please register early.

posts.title: Biomedical Science Research Symposium 2026
posts.excerpt: Faculty and final-year students shared research on antimicrobial resistance, kidney disease and dengue diagnostics.

body.text: Our first Biomedical Science Research Symposium brought together faculty, final-year students and guest speakers from hospital labs.
Talks covered antimicrobial resistance in hospital samples, early markers for kidney disease and faster dengue screening.
Thank you to everyone who joined us. Papers from the day are on the Research filter.

posts.title: Simulation-based training and nursing student confidence in Sri Lanka
posts.excerpt: A study of how simulation sessions affect first-year nursing students’ confidence in core clinical skills before placement.
findings: Confidence in core skills rose after six simulation sessions.
Debrief after each scenario was rated the most useful part.
Students with more simulation hours reported less anxiety on placement.

posts.title: Patient safety practices in private hospital wards
posts.excerpt: A review of everyday safety checks on private hospital wards and where gaps most often appear.
findings: Handover was the step where most gaps appeared.
Wards with a written checklist missed fewer checks.
Night shifts showed lower checklist use.

posts.title: Nurse staffing and burnout: a regional study
posts.excerpt: How nurse-to-patient ratios relate to burnout across hospitals in the Western Province.
findings: Higher patient loads linked to higher burnout scores.
Regular breaks lowered reported exhaustion.
Peer support schemes were rare but valued.

posts.title: Student wellbeing after the transition to university
posts.excerpt: Tracking first-year students’ wellbeing over their first two semesters and what helped them settle in.
findings: Wellbeing dipped most in weeks 6 to 10.
Peer mentoring helped students settle faster.
Students who knew where to get help used it earlier.

posts.title: Mental health stigma among young adults in Sri Lanka
posts.excerpt: A survey of attitudes to mental health and help-seeking among 18 to 25 year olds.
findings: Most respondents would support a friend, fewer would seek help themselves.
Family attitudes strongly shaped help-seeking.
Online information was the most trusted first step.

posts.title: Workplace stress and coping in healthcare staff
posts.excerpt: How doctors, nurses and support staff cope with workplace stress, and which coping styles help most.
findings: Problem-focused coping linked to lower stress.
Support staff reported the least access to help.
Short team debriefs were rated helpful.

posts.title: Antimicrobial resistance patterns in urban hospital samples
posts.excerpt: Resistance patterns in bacterial samples from urban hospitals, and what they mean for first-line treatment.
findings: Resistance to common first-line drugs was rising.
Patterns differed between hospitals.
Regular local testing can guide better prescribing.

posts.title: Biomarkers for early detection of kidney disease
posts.excerpt: Testing urine and blood markers that could flag chronic kidney disease earlier in high-risk communities.
findings: Two urine markers rose before standard tests changed.
Low-cost screening is possible in rural clinics.
Larger follow-up studies are planned.

posts.title: Molecular screening methods for dengue
posts.excerpt: Comparing fast molecular tests for dengue with standard lab methods for speed, cost and accuracy.
findings: Fast tests matched lab accuracy in early infection.
Results were ready in under two hours.
Cost per test fell with batch testing.

posts.title: Digital health adoption in Sri Lankan clinics
posts.excerpt: How private and public clinics are taking up digital records, e-prescriptions and online appointments.
findings: Online appointments were the most common first step.
Staff training was the main barrier.
Patients welcomed digital records when privacy was explained.

posts.title: Patient experience in private outpatient services
posts.excerpt: What patients value most in private outpatient visits, from waiting times to how clearly things are explained.
findings: Clear explanations mattered more than waiting time.
Booking systems cut waits by about a third.
Follow-up calls improved satisfaction.

posts.title: Health literacy among first-time patients
posts.excerpt: Measuring how well first-time patients understand their diagnosis and medicines, and simple ways to help.
findings: Many patients could not repeat their medicine plan.
Picture-based leaflets improved recall.
Teach-back took under two minutes per patient.
